title: Kite3D - AI game engine that runs in your browser
author: invocation02
selftext:
Kite3D is an open source AI game engine that runs in your browser. It is powered by three.js. Its key features are: 

\- AI native: game projects are git repos, so many agents can develop in parallel in worktree branches. there's also a kite3d CLI for agents. 

\- browser editor: a local browser editor allows you to load the project, make changes to the scene, play it, and more. the usual things you expect from a game engine. 

\- entity component system (ECS): Kite3D supports ECS, allowing agents to write data-driven games that are better organized and perform better 

\- hot-reloaded components: watch agent edit your project live in the editor  

One cool thing about kite3D is it allows parallel game dev with agents. To add a new feature, an agent works in a copy of the game project folder (git worktree). To test the feature, the agent just opens a new kite3d editor tab, and runs its copy of the game there. 

You can have 10 agents working on parts of the game at once in their own kite3d editor tab. e.g. if agent adds a new enemy to your game, you can test just that by going to agent's kite3d tab and playing.

Give it a try by telling your agent: 

    use npx kite3d and build me <my game>

  
Repo: [https://github.com/blitzdotdev/kite3d](https://github.com/blitzdotdev/kite3d)

comments.author: mannew2026
comments.body: Can you port games to Nintendo switch using this?

replies.author: invocation02
replies.body: you can use this to reconstruct the game, play it to verify it works, then ask ai to port it to native code for nintendo. keep in mind kite3d games are written in js

replies.author: mannew2026
replies.body: That would become an entire porting project though right? Like Unity for example has this ability to select Nintendo switch as a build output.

replies.author: invocation02
replies.body: Yes. Nintendo switch as build output is not supported in kite3d today
